result.note: Tests the RDIF's institutional home, launch date, funding rules and first cohort of fund managers named in October 2026.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF):
items: It operates within a wider INR 1 trillion scheme managed by NITI Aayog.
Government money can cover at most half of a project or equity funding round.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the wider INR 1 trillion scheme is managed by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, not NITI Aayog. The company or other non-government sources must provide the rest of the funding, which TBB notes can push managers towards faster-to-market startups.
questions.source: The RDIF, launched in November 2025, operates within a wider INR 1 trillion (USD 10.51 billion) scheme managed by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation.

questions.prompt: Consider the following pairs relating to the Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) as described in October 2026:
items: Horizon of RDIF capital from the government — 50 years, interest-free
Minimum technology maturity of funded projects — Technology Readiness Level 4
First cohort of 19 fund managers — 14 alternative investment funds and five focused research organisations
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: All three pairs match the story. Managers fund projects at Technology Readiness Level 4 or above, broadly technologies with laboratory-level prototypes, and the government gives RDIF capital a 50-year, interest-free horizon.
questions.source: The cohort comprises 14 alternative investment funds and five focused research organisations, which are expected to mobilise matching private capital.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the Centre named 19 fund managers to channel money from the Research, Development and Innovation Fund into private research and innovation. How much were they to channel?
questions.explain: The 19 managers would channel INR 71.31 billion (USD 737 million) from the RDIF. INR 1 trillion is the size of the wider scheme managed by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation within which the RDIF operates.
questions.source: On Monday, the Centre said 19 fund managers would channel INR 71.31 billion (USD 737 million) from the Research, Development and Innovation Fund (RDIF) into private research and innovation.
